title: K-flat complexes of module objects
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme, with the small pro-étale site and universe convention of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and let $\mathcal R$ be a commutative ring object [pur713-def-ring-object] of $\mathsf{Sh}(X_{\Proet},\mathsf{Ab})$. Write $\mathcal B=\mathsf{Mod}_{\mathcal R}(X_{\Proet})$ for the category of module objects [pur713-def-modules]. Complexes are unbounded $\mathbf Z$-indexed cochain complexes, with cohomology and quasi-isomorphisms as in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]; acyclic means that every cohomology object is zero. The direct-sum total tensor, formed using the relative tensor product of [pur713-def-relative-tensor], is
$$
(P\otimes_{\mathcal R}N)^n=\bigoplus_{p+q=n}P^p\otimes_{\mathcal R}N^q,
\qquad
 d|_{(p,q)}=d_P^p\otimes1+(-1)^p1\otimes d_N^q.
$$
The two displayed components land in the $(p+1,q)$ and $(p,q+1)$ summands, respectively. A complex $P$ is K-flat if $P\otimes_{\mathcal R}N$ is acyclic for every acyclic complex $N$ of $\mathcal B$. A K-flat resolution of $M$ is a quasi-isomorphism $P\to M$ with $P$ K-flat. Functorial K-flat resolutions exist: there is a functor $Q:\mathrm{CoCh}(\mathcal B)\to\mathrm{CoCh}(\mathcal B)$ and a natural transformation $q:Q\Rightarrow\mathrm{id}$ such that each $Q(M)$ is K-flat and each $q_M$ is a quasi-isomorphism.

proof.text: Start with $\mathsf{Ab}$, viewed as $\mathbf Z$-modules: [lem-weil-pbc-ring-modules-grothendieck-abelian] gives its Grothendieck abelian structure, and [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor] specifies its closed symmetric tensor $\otimes_{\mathbf Z}$. It has a functorial flat cover: for an abelian group $A$, take the free abelian group $F(A)=\bigoplus_{a\in A}\mathbf Z[a]$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module], and send $[a]$ to $a$. For $f:A\to B$ send $[a]$ to $[f(a)]$; identities, composition, and naturality of the augmentation hold on these generators. The augmentation is surjective since $a$ is the image of $[a]$. Each $F(A)$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-projective-module-flat], whose last sentence includes free modules. Thus this is a functor with flat values and a natural epimorphism to the identity.

source.place: The categories of the table; explicit free cover supplying its coefficient-category hypothesis

proof.text: Use the small skeleton in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], in the larger universe specified there, so its indexing category is essentially small relative to the abelian-group values. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-tensor-closed] with $\mathcal A=\mathsf{Ab}$: $\mathcal C=\mathsf{Sh}(X_{\Proet},\mathsf{Ab})$ is Grothendieck abelian and closed symmetric monoidal, its tensor is additive in each variable, and each tensor functor preserves all small colimits. The tensor is the sheafified $\otimes_{\mathbf Z}$, not a pointwise tensor asserted to be already a sheaf. Apply [lem-sfb-sheaf-functorial-flat-resolution] to the free cover of step 1. All its coefficient hypotheses were checked there, so $\mathcal C$ has a functorial flat cover.

source.place: The categories of the table, first three sentences

proof.text: The commutativity of $\mathcal R$ and step 2 allow [lem-sfb-modobj-grothendieck] and [def-sfb-modobj-internal-hom] to apply. Thus $\mathcal B$ is Grothendieck abelian, and $M\otimes_{\mathcal R}-$ has the stated internal-Hom right adjoint. Symmetry is supplied by [def-sfb-modobj-symmetric-tensor]. These use the same balanced coequalizer as [pur713-def-relative-tensor]: both arrows are the two module actions, and that node states that the action induced through $N$ agrees with the action induced through $M$. The identity on the unbalanced tensor therefore induces inverse maps between the two coequalizers, by their universal properties. In particular no replacement of the relative tensor is being assumed. By [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits], each fixed-factor relative tensor preserves all small colimits (use symmetry for the other side). It is additive: it preserves zero and binary coproducts; in an abelian category these are biproducts, with projections determined by identities and zero maps. It consequently preserves the diagonal and codiagonal and hence the formula $f+g=\nabla(f\oplus g)\Delta$.

source.place: Closed module tensor; Grothendieck structure from lem-sfb-modobj-grothendieck.proof.md; elementary comparison of the two specified coequalizers

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-modobj-flat-resolutions] to $\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal R$. Step 2 supplies all its ambient hypotheses, including the functorial flat cover. It supplies a functorial flat cover in $\mathcal B$, explicitly $M\mapsto\mathcal R\otimes F_{\mathcal C}(M)$ with augmentation $\gamma_M\circ(1\otimes\pi_M)$. Here $M$ inside $F_{\mathcal C}$ denotes its underlying abelian sheaf. The cited statement asserts both flatness for the relative tensor and that the augmentation is a natural epimorphism; neither property is inferred merely from the definition of flatness.

source.place: Free modules on the functorial flat cover, and the natural epimorphism

proof.text: The direct sums in the displayed total tensor exist because $\mathcal B$ is Grothendieck abelian [lem-sfb-modobj-grothendieck], and so has small colimits. The differentials and maps are defined on each summand by the displayed formula, using the additive tensor from step 3. On a $(p,q)$ summand, the square of the differential has pure terms $d_P^{p+1}d_P^p\otimes1$ and $1\otimes d_N^{q+1}d_N^q$, both zero by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]; the mixed terms have coefficients $(-1)^p$ and $(-1)^{p+1}$ and cancel. Tensoring cochain maps degreewise commutes with this differential, and identities and composition hold on each summand. This gives exactly the direct-sum total tensor used in [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso].

source.place: Direct-sum total tensor convention, with explicit differential-square verification

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-kflat-derivability] to $\mathcal B$. Step 3 supplies its Grothendieck abelian and additive monoidal structure and preservation of all small colimits by either tensor functor; step 4 supplies its functorial flat cover. The cited statement gives a functor $Q$ on the category of unbounded cochain complexes and a natural quasi-isomorphism $q:Q\Rightarrow\mathrm{id}$ with two-sided K-flat values in the sense of [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso]. To check precisely the one-sided acyclic-test definition in this item, take acyclic $N$. Then $N\to0$ is a quasi-isomorphism, since in each degree its cohomology map is $0\to0$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Tensoring it with $Q(M)$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Its target is zero: relative tensor preserves the initial object by step 3, and all summands of the total tensor with the zero complex are zero. Hence $H^n(Q(M)\otimes_{\mathcal R}N)=0$ for every $n$. Thus each $q_M$ is a K-flat resolution in exactly the asserted sense. The functor and naturality are on complexes, as required, with no claim of a functorial choice on the homotopy category.

source.place: First three sentences, with hypotheses supplied in steps 1–4 and the acyclic-test consequence expanded

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q47-a6c9f9140 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole delivery. It is one commit with two files: the item and the report. There are no new nodes and nothing needed fixing. Statement: it keeps the main-20261015 order-2484 definition exactly (one-sided acyclic test with P on the left, resolution direction P→M, any commutative ring object, unbounded complexes). It adds only the conventions that were implicit: the site and universes from def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, the cochain conventions from def-weil-abstract-derived-category, and the signed direct-sum differential, which matches def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso and Stacks 06YN. The existence claim is now stated precisely as a functor Q on CoCh(B) with a natural quasi-isomorphism Q⇒id. Nothing is weakened, and module objects are not silently identified with sheaves of O-modules. Steps: (1) Ab is Grothendieck abelian with a functorial free flat cover; additivity of ⊗_Z is used but not written, which is elementary. (2) The pro-étale site is essentially small via the V-small skeleton; lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-tensor-closed applies, and lem-sfb-sheaf-functorial-flat-resolution's hypotheses all hold. (3) lem-sfb-modobj-grothendieck and the internal-Hom node apply. def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor coequalizes the same pair of arrows as pur713-def-relative-tensor, and the R-actions agree by that node's own clause, so the two relative tensors are the same. Colimit preservation and additivity of the module tensor are argued correctly. (4) lem-sfb-modobj-flat-resolutions states exactly what the step uses. (5) I checked d²=0 and the signs myself; the step is correctly marked elementary. (6) lem-sfb-kflat-derivability's hypotheses are met; its two-sided K-flat values give the acyclic-test K-flat property because Q(M)⊗N→Q(M)⊗0=0 is a quasi-isomorphism. Route: the unit has no steps and this is not its key node. I accept all five declared tool uses as generic categorical black boxes. The other off-unit statements cited are Mathlib leaves. Integrity: no cycle (closure of 308 nodes), every cited id exists and none is merged, and no SGA source is used. Duplicates: def-pc-kflat-complex, def-weil-derived-tensor and def-pc-module-kflat-complex are over other coefficient categories, and lem-pd-module-ringed-topos-derived-comparison treats this item and def-pc-kflat-complex as separate notions, so same_as=[] is fine. Edge cases checked: X empty, R=0, the zero complexes, unbounded complexes, characteristic 2.
